label: Kyriba claim boundary
query: If Kyriba is not live yet, what exactly can Lakeshore claim today without overstating value?
answer: You can safely claim Kyriba as a committed, progressing initiative — not a live value engine yet. I’d frame it in three tight layers: 1) What you can say as fact today “Lakeshore has completed strategy, vendor selection, and BAFO for a Kyriba-centered treasury modernization (initiative LSH-KYRIBA-TREASURY-2026).” “Kyriba has been approved as the target SaaS treasury platform; we are in pre‑implementation planning and integration design.” “Scope coverage includes cash visibility, bank connectivity, and core treasury workflows, with architecture aligned to our Azure and MuleSoft integration patterns.” These are all backed by the artifact spine and approved stages (Strategy through BAFO). 2) What you can say about expected value (future‑tense, conditional) Use language like: “We expect Kyriba to enable…” rather than “Kyriba delivers today…” “We expect improved daily cash visibility and standardized treasury processes once Kyriba is implemented and cut over.” “We anticipate reductions in manual reconciliations and better control over bank connectivity, subject to successful deployment and adoption.” Tie any numbers (if you use them) explicitly to the business case, e.g. “per our approved business case, the projected benefit is…” — not as realized savings. 3) What you must avoid claiming right now No “is live,” “is in production,” “is delivering X savings,” or “has de‑risked treasury operations” language — Executive Decision, Selection (final), Transition, and Value are still in review/needs‑review. No implications that integrations, controls, or operating‑model changes are complete; those are downstream of the current stage.Evidence checked: intake.tenant_context (loaded tenant context), telemetry.value_attestation (verified versus projected value), intake.missing_fields (missing or stale evidence fields), intake.question_scope (question scope).
